text:
emily: FYI we received VendorCloud's Q1 credit memo today. It shows a $45,600 vendor rebate tied to committed GPU hours that were under-delivered last quarter. Vendor wants to net it against our next payout but vendor ops says we should accrue it now. Thoughts?
jamal: Do we have the underlying statement? link: https://drive.redwood/rebates/VendorCloud_Q1_281234.pdf
renee: If the credit is for past under-delivery it sounds like a reduction of cost of goods sold, so we should book an accrual/contra-expense for March close. But cash treatment vs revenue impact needs review.
tom: For month-end I need exact accounting entries. Can we do: 
```
Dr Vendor Rebates Receivable 45,600
Cr Accrued Vendor Rebates 45,600
```
then when settled: 
```
Dr Cash/Payable 0 (net)
Dr Accrued Vendor Rebates 45,600
Cr COGS 45,600
```
Is that acceptable?
emily: That works, but audit asked earlier this month to only accrue when credit is both probable and estimable. Vendor ops confirmed the memo is signed and scheduled to apply on next payout. Probable + estimable = yes.
jamal: One extra wrinkle: the rebate is partially attributable to customers on reserved capacity where we passed through vendor hours. That affects revenue gross-up calculations and deferred revenue amort schedules for those customers. We need to map the $45.6k to product buckets.
renee: Good catch. If we passed vendor cost through to customers, the rebate reduces cost and may increase margin but does not change our revenue unless we adjust pass-through pricing. For revenue recognition, only if we change the standalone selling price for future invoices would transaction price allocation change. But we still need to update cost accruals tied to the revenue schedule dimensions.
tom: How about we split the $45,600 across two buckets: hosted_shared = $28,000 and dedicated_reserved = $17,600 based on usage report. I'll attach the usage calc.
emily: Perfect. For the close checklist: please create two accrual JEs today and tag them with rev_schedule refs so reconciliation team can update unit economics analytics.
close-bot: New JE request received: ref JE-2026-03-VC1. Approver required: @jamal.
jamal: Approved. Posting now. JE: 
```
JE-2026-03-VC1
Dr Vendor Rebates Receivable - hosted_shared 28,000 (dim: rev_sched_hosted_shared)
Dr Vendor Rebates Receivable - dedicated_reserved 17,600 (dim: rev_sched_ded_reserved)
Cr Accrued Vendor Rebates 45,600
```
renee: After posting, finance ops pls push an entry to the close tracker and update the deferred revenue feed with a note that COGS will be adjusted for pass-through customers.
emily: Finance ops team: also check whether any of those customers received pricing experiment discounts in Feb — if so, the rebate allocation to those customers may need re-evaluation.
jamal: I queried billing: cohort IDs 7,8 impacted by the Feb experiment. Creating a list in /shared/close/Q1_vendor_rebates.csv.
tom: Once rebate entries are live, I'll run the unit economics P&L refresh and tag product analytics. Expect margin delta report in ~2 hours.
audit-bot: Reminder: retain vendor memo and email trail for 7 years. Attachments required: vendor memo, usage calc, approval chain.
emily: I'll upload docs to SFDC opp 00599 and attach to the JE. Closing note: posting accrual preserves audit trail and avoids retroactive revenue edits. If vendor instead nets on payout, we'll reverse the accrual when cash is applied. :white_check_mark:
